> **What this case shows** — the [sibling case](../sway-cognition-kendall-bds/index.qmd) found that slower
> cognitive processing tracks more postural sway (Spearman rho = 0.53), but warned that *age* drives both.
> Here we adjust for it. Each subject's sway comes from the **certified** `swayMetrics`; the
> **newly-authored** `partialCorrelation` computes the rank partial correlation of sway and Trail Making
> Test A **controlling for age**, reproducing the **`ppcor`** package and an independent closed-form
> recompute to **machine precision**. The association **attenuates to 0.20** (p=0.012, still significant but
> much weaker), and the *linear* partial correlation **vanishes** (0.05, p=0.55): **most of the marginal
> link was age** — though a modest rank association survives.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — assemble `(x, y, covariate)` per subject → `partialCorrelation(x, y, z, method="spearman")`.
**Way of thinking** — a marginal correlation can be a mirage of a shared cause. Before reading a link as
real, remove the obvious confound and see what survives. The honest answer here is "mostly age, a little
not" — and saying so is the point.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioMoCap::swayMetrics()`, `PhysioAnalysis::partialCorrelation()`.
:::

## Proposition

Controlling for age, the rank partial correlation of eyes-closed-foam sway and Trail Making Test A time is
0.201 (p=0.012, df=155) — down from a marginal Spearman rho of 0.532 — while the Pearson partial correlation
is 0.048 (p=0.55); `partialCorrelation` reproduces `ppcor::pcor.test` and a closed-form recompute to machine
precision.

## Question & goal

**The question is whether an association survives its obvious confound.** The sibling case certified the
marginal cognitive-motor link and explicitly deferred the age adjustment; this fold performs it, authoring
the partial-correlation op and resolving the open question.

## Challenge & approach

We take each subject's eyes-closed-foam COP path length (from `swayMetrics`, certified against the Prieto
reference in the [sway-posturography-bds](../sway-posturography-bds/index.qmd) case), Trail Making Test A
time, and age, and compute `partialCorrelation` (rank / Spearman) of sway and TMT-A controlling for age —
checking it against `ppcor::pcor.test` and an independent closed-form recompute, and comparing with the
marginal correlation and the Pearson partial.

```
158 subjects: sway (swayMetrics, certified), TMT-A, age
  marginal Spearman(sway, TMT-A)        = 0.532
  partial  Spearman(sway, TMT-A | age)  = 0.201   (p = 0.012, df = 155)   <- attenuated, survives
  partial  Pearson (sway, TMT-A | age)  = 0.048   (p = 0.55)              <- vanishes
     vs ppcor::pcor.test        → |diff| ~ 2e-16 (machine precision)
     vs closed-form recompute   → |diff| ~ 3e-16 (Pearson: bit-for-bit)
```

## Data

**Santos & Duarte (2016) BDS balance dataset (figshare)**: per subject, eyes-closed-foam COP path length,
Trail Making Test A time, and age, for the 158 subjects with all three. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: the correlation of sway with cognitive speed before and after adjusting for age — the marginal Spearman rho (0.53) drops to a rank partial correlation of 0.20 (p=0.012), and the linear partial correlation to 0.05 (p=0.55, non-significant). Right: the added-variable plot — sway and TMT-A ranks after age is removed from both; the weak residual slope is what survives adjustment.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* left — the tall marginal bar collapses once age is partialled out; the surviving rank
bar is small but not zero. Right — the added-variable scatter is the partial correlation made visible: after
age is regressed out of both, only a faint upward trend remains.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| marginal Spearman | 0.532 |
| **partial Spearman \| age** | **0.201** (p = 0.012) |
| partial Pearson \| age | 0.048 (p = 0.55, ns) |
| df | 155 |
| n | 158 |
| vs `ppcor::pcor.test` (\|diff\|) | **< 1e-9** (~2e-16) |
| vs closed-form recompute (\|diff\|) | **< 1e-9** (Pearson bit-for-bit) |

The partial correlation equals both references to machine precision. Values trace to
[`artifacts/sway_cognition_partial_summary.csv`](artifacts/sway_cognition_partial_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`partialCorrelation` reproduces the reference on the certified `swayMetrics`. The transferable takeaway:
**partial out the confound before you believe a correlation. Here it converts a striking marginal link
(rho = 0.53) into an honest one — mostly age, with a modest rank association (0.20) surviving. A significant
slope with a small partial correlation is a real-but-minor effect against a dominant confound; report it
that way.**

## Open questions

- Age adjustment leaves a modest but significant rank partial correlation (0.20); whether it reflects a
  direct cognitive-motor pathway or residual confounding by other age-linked factors (medication,
  comorbidity, sensory loss) needs a fuller multivariable model and, ideally, a dual-task or longitudinal
  design. The single-covariate partial correlation is the honest first adjustment. *Documented, not
  escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| Posturography sway metrics | `swayMetrics()` | PhysioMoCap |
| Partial correlation (control a confound) | `partialCorrelation()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| Marginal correlation (Pearson/Spearman/Kendall) | `correlationTest()`, `kendallTau()` | PhysioAnalysis |

**Reading the result.**

- **partial vs marginal** — the drop from marginal to partial is how much of the association the covariate
  explains; here age explains most of it.
- **rank vs linear partial** — with skewed variables the rank (Spearman) partial is the fair test; that the
  Pearson partial vanishes while the rank partial survives says the residual link is monotonic, not linear.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioMoCap); library(PhysioAnalysis)

sway <- vapply(subjects, function(s) swayMetrics(cop[[s]], 100)$path_length, numeric(1))
partialCorrelation(sway, tmt_time, age, method = "spearman")  # partial r, p, df -- machine-precision vs ppcor
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/sway_cognition_partial_summary.csv`](artifacts/sway_cognition_partial_summary.csv), and
[`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks the partial correlations (rank and linear), their p-values and df, the
machine-precision match against ppcor and the closed-form recompute, the attenuation relative to the
marginal, the sample size, and the honestly noted scope (authors the new partialCorrelation op; sway from
the certified swayMetrics; mostly age-confounded; one covariate; cross-sectional association).
